headline: Inyo National Forest Permits and Seasonal Road Access
reservation: Wilderness permits are required year-round for overnight stays in Inyo National Forest and neighboring parks; many popular trailheads use a quota system from May to November. A lodging or glamping reservation does not provide trail access or bypass road closures. Systems for high-demand areas like Mt. Whitney or overnight backpacking often require lottery participation months in advance; always verify current procedures on the official Recreation.gov site.

days.title: Granite Spires and Ancient Basins

stops.name: Alabama Hills
stops.detail: Walk the Mobius Arch Loop to see the Sierra Crest framed by rounded granite formations.

stops.name: Manzanar National Historic Site
stops.detail: Explore the preserved grounds and visitor center to understand the history of this WWII Japanese American incarceration camp.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local valley travel; conditions vary by wind.
days.note: Low elevation heat in summer; seek shade by midday.

days.title: High Alpine Lakes and Canyons

stops.name: Bishop Creek Canyon
stops.detail: Drive toward Lake Sabrina or South Lake for high-altitude scenery and aspen groves.

stops.name: Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest
stops.detail: Travel to the White Mountains to see the world's oldest living trees at over 10,000 feet elevation.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours; steep mountain grades require brake monitoring.
days.note: Check road status for Schulman Grove, typically open May through October.

days.title: Tufa Towers and Volcanic Rims

stops.name: Mono Lake Tufa State Natural Reserve
stops.detail: Walk the South Tufa trail to see unique limestone spires rising from the saline lake.

stops.name: Hot Creek Geological Site
stops.detail: View steaming turquoise pools and fumaroles set against a dramatic canyon backdrop.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; heavy snow may block secondary routes in winter.
days.note: Stay on boardwalks to avoid hazardous geothermal activity.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking at Mosquito Flat and Whitney Portal fills early during summer weekends. Have a secondary destination planned if main lots are restricted.

intel.title: Cellular Dead Zones
intel.text: Service is generally reliable in Bishop and Mammoth but disappears quickly in mountain canyons. Download offline maps before leaving Highway 395.

intel.title: Valley Supply Points
intel.text: Gas is readily available in Lone Pine, Bishop, and Lee Vining. Distances between stations increase significantly when heading into the White Mountains or deep canyons.

intel.title: Autumn Foliage Peaks
intel.text: Aspen color typically moves from high elevations in late September to lower canyons by mid-October. Monitor local color reports as timing varies annually.

intel.title: Tioga Pass Transitions
intel.text: Highway 120 into Yosemite is a seasonal route and usually closes following the first significant autumn snow. Check Caltrans for gate status before planning a crossing.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at BIH or nearby hubs; Bishop is the primary supply center for groceries and bear canisters before heading to mountain cabins.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars suit Highway 395; high-clearance 4WD is recommended for unpaved Alabama Hills spurs. Check rental terms for off-pavement use.
plan.goldenHour: Minaret Vista near Mammoth Lakes offers a dramatic sunset view of the Ritter Range, depending on seasonal gate access.
